one_liner: A founder's CRM that fits on one keyboard-driven page — pipeline, notes, and email in sub-100ms.
description: dealpage is a CRM for founders doing their own sales. The entire pipeline lives on a single keyboard-navigable page: move deals, log notes, and send synced email without touching the mouse or configuring a single workflow. It imports from HubSpot and Pipedrive in minutes and refuses to grow admin screens.
target_user: Founders and first sales hires at early-stage startups

icp.who: Founders at pre-seed to Series A B2B startups running 10-100 active deals themselves
icp.pain: HubSpot and Salesforce are built for sales ops teams; founders end up tracking deals in Notion or spreadsheets because real CRMs feel like ERP software
icp.buying_trigger: Deal volume outgrows the Notion table right as a fundraise or first sales hire demands a real pipeline view

differentiators: Every action is keyboard-first and lands in under 100ms — built like Linear, not like Salesforce
Zero setup: no pipelines to configure, no required fields, no admin console
Two-way Gmail sync included in the base price, not an add-on
proof_points: Founders at 40 companies use it as their primary CRM
Customer quote on site: migrated 12,000 contacts out of HubSpot in one afternoon
p95 interaction latency under 100ms, measured and published on the site

voice.sample_phrase: Your pipeline on one page. Your hands never leave the keyboard.

signals: Stripe billing live for beta customers

confidence.notes: Positioning and latency claims are consistent and specific. Customer counts are small-sample and self-reported.
